freeze_procedure: An independent reviewer inspects this file, the code and the pre-freeze receipts before any outcome exists; the coordinator sets status to 'frozen_pre_outcome', frozen_before_outcomes to true and frozen_at, commits, and then writes receipts/freeze-record.json (template: receipts/freeze-record.template.json) with the sha256 of the committed protocol.json bytes and commits it. evaluate.py takes the expected sha256 only from that record, verifies every pin and a clean git tree for this directory, and refuses otherwise before it reads a price.
question: Does the Frazzini-Lamont earnings announcement premium, with announcement dates from SEC 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance times, exist in US common stocks from 2017-01 to 2026-08, and does its tradable long leg beat SPY after measured costs?
evidence_label: HIST (real SEC metadata and daily bars); SYN for tests

facts_confirmed_in_extracted_text: p.8: using last year's announcement months, 80% of announcements fall in the expected month; restricting to firms with at least 4 announcements in the previous calendar year raises accuracy to 93%
p.9: buy expected announcers and short non-announcers on the last trading day of month t-1, hold to the last day of month t, value weighted
p.9: sample restricted to firms with exactly 4 earnings announcements in the previous 12 calendar months
p.10: the long-short portfolio earns 61 basis points per month with a t-statistic over 5 (1973-2004)
stocks with predictably high announcement volume earn 1.5% per month; the premium is not concentrated in small stocks (NYSE-breakpoint size deciles)
footnote 2: probability that the actual annual announcement month equals the expected (prior-year) month ranges from 61.28% (October) to 81.69% (December); February 76.94%
US 1991-2010 long-short 75.9 basis points per month
Table 4 minimum: at least ten firms on each side of a monthly long-short portfolio

heitz_narayanamoorthy_zekhnini.status: abstract not retrieved in this worktree (fetch failed); the claim that the US premium disappeared after 2004 and moved to 8-K filing dates is carried from the task brief, unverified here
heitz_narayanamoorthy_zekhnini.use: context only, unverified; it is not a prior of any item, test or threshold

announcements.source: SEC data.sec.gov/submissions CIK##########.json plus filings.files continuations; fields form, items, acceptanceDateTime, filingDate, reportDate, accessionNumber
announcements.definition: original 8-K (form exactly '8-K') whose comma-separated items include '2.02'; 8-K/A excluded and counted
announcements.acceptance_clock: acceptanceDateTime is UTC (Z) and is converted to America/New_York; collect_edgar.py tzcheck found the converted value equal to the SGML <ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME> header (Eastern) for 24 of 24 sampled 8-Ks and the unconverted digits equal for 0 of 24 (receipts/tzcheck-summary.json); values without Z are refused
announcements.effective_session: the acceptance date when it is a session and the acceptance is before 16:00 ET; otherwise the next session
announcements.merge_rule: after sorting by effective session, a filing within 7 calendar days after a kept announcement is merged into it
announcements.calendar: session dates of the daily dataset with at least 1000 symbols, preceded by NYSE 2015 sessions (weekdays minus 9 listed full holidays)
announcements.identity: CIK to ticker from the current SEC company_tickers.json; ticker '-' normalised to '.'; a CIK enters when a normalised ticker is a daily-dataset symbol; all its matched symbols are securities of the firm

expectation.decision_session: D(t) = last session of calendar month t-1; positions are entered at D(t)'s close and held to the close of the last session of month t
expectation.information_cutoff: filings accepted strictly before 16:00 ET on the session before D(t)
expectation.primary_monthly_rule: eligible when exactly 4 known announcements have effective months in t-12..t-1; expected announcer when one of those is in month t-12; eligible and not expected = non-announcer

secondary_event_time_rule.fiscal_period_assignment: each known announcement is assigned the latest period end (reportDate of a known 10-Q, 10-K or 10-KT, originals only) strictly before its effective session and at most 100 days earlier
secondary_event_time_rule.target_period: latest assigned period end plus 3 months (end-of-month clipped)
secondary_event_time_rule.reference: the known announcement assigned to target minus 12 months within 10 days (52/53-week years)
secondary_event_time_rule.trade: for main-lane eligible firms at D(t), with the expectation formed at month t's cutoff: enter at the close K=5 sessions before the first session on or after the expected date when that entry session lies in month t after D(t); no trade when an announcement accepted after the cutoff has an effective session on or before entry; exit at the close of the session after the effective session of the first later announcement; if there is none by expected date + 30 days, exit at the close of the first session on or after that date; benchmark SPY over the same window when SPY is in the dataset
secondary_event_time_rule.accuracy_match: for date-prediction accuracy only, the actual announcement is the first later announcement assigned to the target period within 10 days (uses later 10-Q/10-K filings)

universe.returns_from: all_c (split, dividend and spin-off adjusted close); raw_c and raw_v for membership only
universe.membership_inputs: raw close of the last bar before D(t), median of raw_c*raw_v over the bars among the 20 sessions before D(t), and a bar on D(t)

common_stock_heuristic.basis: mover-early-entry candidates.py derivative exclusion plus preferred-share suffixes; combined with the CIK map and the exactly-4 Item 2.02 rule, which removes funds and trusts that do not report quarterly earnings on 8-K

universe.weights: confirmatory: prior-20 median dollar volume (market-capitalisation proxy) capped at 2% per name and renormalised (effective cap max(2%, 1/n), excess redistributed pro rata, iterated); applied separately to each portfolio (long, short, top tercile); equal weight and uncapped dollar-volume weight are descriptive
universe.benchmark: SPY: all_c close at D(t) to all_c close on the last session of month t, from the same daily dataset; a month without both SPY closes is invalid for EAP-2..4
universe.descriptive_sample_market: M_t = weighted return of all main-lane eligible symbols (Frazzini-Lamont's sample market); descriptive only, because M contains the long leg: L - M = (1 - w_L)(L - S) duplicates EAP-1 and is not a tradable hedge

EAP-2.hypothesis: mean monthly return of the expected-announcer long leg in excess of SPY > 0

EAP-4.hypothesis: mean monthly net excess of the EAP-2 long leg over SPY after modelled costs > 0
EAP-4.equivalence: net mean > 0 is break-even cost per unit turnover above the turnover-weighted measured cost; both are reported

EAP-1.hypothesis: mean monthly long-short return (expected announcers minus non-announcers, main lane) > 0
EAP-1.role: the published premium, gross of costs and borrow

EAP-3.hypothesis: mean monthly excess over SPY of the top tercile of expected announcers by mean |announcement-session return| over their 4 known prior announcements > 0
EAP-3.proxy: announcement-session return = all_c(effective session) / all_c(previous bar) - 1, from bars before D(t); at least 3 of the 4 prior announcements must have it; tercile = floor(n/3) highest proxies among the month's expected announcers
EAP-3.role: extreme-mover proxy subset (replaces Frazzini-Lamont's announcement-volume sort)

items.invalid_months: a month whose portfolio is below its minimum count, or lacks SPY closes for EAP-2..4, is invalid for that item: it is excluded from the series, never entered as 0

statistics.test: one-sided Student t on the monthly series with Newey-West (Bartlett) standard errors, 4 lags, df = n - 1; 3 and 12 lags reported as sensitivity

primary.method: fixed sequence at alpha 0.05: EAP-2 first; EAP-4 is tested only if EAP-2 is rejected
primary.adoption: intersection-union: adopt only if both EAP-2 and EAP-4 are rejected

multiplicity.note: the two families are separate; secondary results never change the adoption decision

minimum_samples.per_month: EAP-1 needs at least 10 long and 10 short symbols; EAP-2 and EAP-4 at least 10 long symbols and both SPY closes; EAP-3 at least 30 long symbols carrying the proxy (at least 10 in the tercile) and both SPY closes
minimum_samples.below_minimum: the item is reported inconclusive and not rejected; in the primary sequence an inconclusive EAP-2 stops the sequence; in Holm its p-value enters as 1.0

mde.formula: MDE = (t_{1-alpha,n-1} + t_{0.80,n-1}) * sigma / sqrt(n), n = 116, one-sided, NW inflation ignored
mde.sigma_assumption: 2.39%/month, the upper bound of Frazzini-Lamont's own long-short SD (61 bp with t > 5 over 384 months); for our series (a long leg over SPY with capped dollar-volume weights, 2017-2026) it should be read as a lower bound of the relevant SD, so every MDE here is optimistic; no outcome of this study was used
mde.consequence: the adoption items are underpowered for an effect of about 0.4%/month; a non-rejection is not evidence of absence

upper_bound_reporting.bound: one-sided 95% upper confidence bound = mean + t_{0.95,n-1} * NW(4) se, reported for every item
upper_bound_reporting.realized_mde: X = (t_{0.95,n-1} + t_{0.80,n-1}) * NW(4) se of the item's realized series
upper_bound_reporting.wording_when_not_rejected: not rejected at the preregistered level; the design had 80% power only above ≈X%/month, so an effect of the published size is not ruled out

segments.design: one confirmatory pass over 2017-01..2026-08 (116 months) with descriptive calendar-year reporting
segments.justification: every parameter is fixed from the literature before outcomes (no tuning, so no development split is needed); a split would cut a 116-month sample whose MDE already exceeds the published effect; the question is the post-2004 existence of the premium over the full available period
segments.why_2017: the daily dataset starts 2016-01-04 and the monthly rule needs the 12 prior months

costs.rebalance: monthly at D(t)'s close; turnover = sum |w_new - w_old_drifted| over the long leg; the first month buys from cash; the final holdings are not charged a closing sale
costs.fees: blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/data/fees-v3.json: SEC Section 31 (usd_per_million of sale notional, by trade date) plus FINRA TAF (usd_per_share / price per dollar sold; per-trade cap ignored, conservative); commission 0
not_modelled: short-leg borrow and short rebates (EAP-1 is a gross paper premium)
the SPY hedge's own trading cost
closing-auction pricing that is usually tighter than the quoted spread

half_spread_table.confirmatory: data/cost-table-eap-v1.json (pinned): measured closing half-spreads on D(t) sessions, main lane, 4 dollar-volume tiers [1,5)M [5,50)M [50,500)M >=500M x 3 price tiers [5,20) [20,100) >=100; 5%-trimmed mean per cell, cells with n < 30 use their dollar-volume tier pooled
half_spread_table.measurement: spreads.py: stratified deterministic sample of main-lane (symbol, D(t)) pairs by year x dollar-volume tier x price tier (25 per cell), Alpaca SIP quotes 15:55-16:00 ET (12:55-13:00 on early closes) newest valid quote

sensitivity_half_spread_table_mover_v1.source: blueprints/us-equities/mover-early-entry/evidence/cost-table-run-v1.json, time bucket 10:00-16:01 ET (index 3), price tier bounds [2,5,20], dollar-volume tier bounds [1e6,5e6]

main_lane.from_cell: 3|2|1 used instead of 3|3|1 (0.00202, a fallback cell with n=17): conservative

sensitivity_half_spread_table_mover_v1.role: sensitivity only: EAP-4 net series recomputed with it and reported descriptively

descriptive_only: L - M against the sample market (duplicates EAP-1 scaled by 1 - w_L)
uncapped dollar-volume and equal-weighted versions of EAP-1 and EAP-2
small-cap lane versions of EAP-1 and EAP-2
EAP-4 with the mover-v1 half-spread table
all items with NW 3 and 12 lags
event-time secondary trades (main lane): count, mean and median return and return minus SPY
break-even cost per unit turnover versus the turnover-weighted measured cost
delisting and data flags: no_decision_close, no_bar_in_month, bars_end_early

decision_rule.adopt_for_pre_positioning_research: EAP-2 and EAP-4 both rejected in the primary fixed sequence
decision_rule.long_short_premium_only: EAP-2 not rejected, EAP-1 rejected under the secondary Holm
decision_rule.no_evidence_underpowered: neither EAP-2 nor EAP-1 rejected; reported with the upper-bound wording in statistics.upper_bound_reporting
decision_rule.extreme_mover_targeting: EAP-3 rejected supports sizing toward past extreme announcement reactions; it is not a standalone adoption

pre_freeze_allowed_on_real_data: SEC filing metadata collection and counts
lane membership counts from raw close and raw volume before each decision session
closing-quote half-spreads on D(t) sessions (15:55-16:00 ET quotes only)
survivorship counts of main-lane-qualifying daily symbols without a current CIK
per-month maximum weight and effective N from pre-D(t) inputs
counts of firm-months by number of known Item 2.02 events
pre_freeze_forbidden: any return, P&L, hit rate or post-decision price change, or anything derived from them, including sanity checks
announcement-session returns (EAP-3 proxy) on real data

deviations.what: announcement dates are SEC 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance sessions, not Compustat/Bloomberg report dates
deviations.why: point-in-time, timestamped primary source; post-2004 Item 2.02 is mandatory for earnings releases, but it also covers preliminary results and other results-of-operations disclosures (the exactly-4 rule removes most such firms)

deviations.what: weights are prior-20 median dollar volume capped at 2% per name, not market capitalisation
deviations.why: shares outstanding are not in the daily dataset; dollar volume over-weights high-turnover names (Frazzini-Lamont find a larger premium there), so the cap limits concentration; receipts/weights.json gives the per-month maximum weight and effective N

deviations.what: identity from the current SEC ticker map and a current-ticker daily dataset
deviations.why: no point-in-time ticker history is available; issuers delisted or renamed before retrieval drop out. receipts/survivorship.json counts, per decision session, the common-like main-lane-qualifying daily symbols without a current CIK. The bias is unsigned: the missing names include failures and acquired firms (often positive returns) as well as funds and ADRs that would never qualify

deviations.what: returns from Alpaca all-adjusted closes; no delisting returns
deviations.why: CRSP is unavailable; a symbol whose bars stop in the holding month keeps its return to its last bar and then holds cash

deviations.what: common-stock heuristic from symbol patterns, not CRSP share codes 10/11
information cutoff at 16:00 ET the session before D(t)
deviations.why: a decision at D(t)'s close cannot use filings accepted during D(t) and remain implementable; the count window therefore loses at most the last session of t-1

deviations.what: Item 2.02 filings within 7 days merged; 8-K/A excluded
deviations.why: corrections and re-furnished releases would otherwise break the exactly-4 count

deviations.what: early-close days treated as 16:00 closes; 2015 sessions from a listed NYSE holiday set
deviations.why: the dataset has no close times and starts in 2016; affects filings accepted 13:00-16:00 on a few half-days

deviations.what: costs from a measured closing half-spread table (pinned) plus fees-v3; the mover-v1 table only as a sensitivity; borrow, the hedge's cost and impact not modelled
deviations.why: the D(t) close is the rebalancing point; quoted spreads overstate closing-auction costs

deviations.what: EAP-3 sorts on past |announcement-session return| instead of announcement volume
deviations.why: the study targets extreme movers; Frazzini-Lamont's 1.5%/month volume result is the analogous published subset

deviations.what: 116 months, underpowered at the published effect size
deviations.why: the dataset starts in 2016; see statistics.mde

deviations.what: direct stdlib HTTP against data.sec.gov submissions instead of EdgarTools; the signal module is eap_signal.py
deviations.why: EdgarTools is installed only in an isolated Python 3.13 environment; the submissions JSON is the primary source it wraps, and direct access keeps exact raw bytes for the sha256 manifest and exact rate control (<= 8 requests/s)

deviations.what: EAP-2..4 are measured against SPY, not Frazzini-Lamont's sample value-weighted market
deviations.why: the sample market contains the long leg (L - M = (1 - w_L)(L - S)), so it duplicates EAP-1 and is not a tradable hedge

deviations.what: the measured cost table pools 2016-2026 closing quotes and applies one time-invariant half-spread per tier cell to every month
deviations.why: per-year cells would be too thin; the by-year tier medians stay recorded with the table, and EAP-4 with year-specific costs is not a preregistered item

pins.note: sha256 of code, reference data and private inputs; evaluate.run() verifies every entry before any price is read (paths: code and data/ relative to this directory, fees-v3.json under blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/data/, private inputs under the private root and the daily dataset path passed as --daily); regenerate with evaluate.py --print-pins after any code change before the freeze; filings.jsonl.gz is pinned as its compressed file bytes, while receipts/collection-summary.json records the sha256 of its decompressed content
